related_questions.question: How do I get a free first aid kit from FEMA?
related_questions.snippet: The Emergency Financial First Aid Kit is available for free from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). Call (800) 480–2520 and ask for publication number P-2063. It is also available as a free download online at: www.ready.gov/financialpreparedness and at www.operationhope.org.

related_questions.snippet: Capabilities to Reach the Goal The National Preparedness Goal describes five mission areas — prevention, protection, mitigation, response and recovery — and 32 activities, called core capabilities, that address the greatest risks to the nation. Each of these core capabilities is tied to a capability target.

list.title: FEMA Basic Academy:
list.snippet: Courses offered through the Basic Academy at the National Emergency Training Center are also free of charge, and some individuals may be eligible for stipend reimbursement for travel and lodging.

list.title: Who can take them?
list.snippet: The free courses are generally open to anyone who wishes to learn more about emergency management, including those with professional responsibilities and the general public.

list.title: Purpose of the courses:
list.snippet: These courses cover a wide range of topics related to emergency management, including risk assessment, logistics, and general preparedness. They are designed to be helpful in both emergency situations and for general knowledge.

list.title: Certifications:
list.snippet: While the courses themselves are free, you may need to register for a FEMA Student Identification Number (SID) to take the quizzes and earn a certificate.
